baseline: A/R0 bounded live body buffer plus authoritative log recovery
candidate: A/R1 live hint plus authoritative log recovery, no per-recipient live body buffer
required: all accepted obligations complete by audit
finite resource bounds during slow interval
adoption: Prefer simpler R0 if R1 has no material benefit. R1 should reduce live buffering or recovery completion materially (25 percent memory or 20 percent recovery improvement), while normal p95 and stack CPU do not regress more than 20 percent. Report tradeoffs and replicate variation; do not average run p99 as pooled p99.
scope: One Windows native laptop. No broker or physical failure-domain claims. A is sufficient unless measurements demonstrate a reason for C. No implementation of optional cache, relay, N1, replica or speculative experiments merely to fill a matrix.
timestamps: One Python process perf_counter_ns domain for scheduled SEND, response completion and after-SQLite-COMMIT events. DB storedAt is not a commit cursor or latency clock.
notes: Completed latency quantiles always accompany missing/rejected/unresolved counts. Slow-recipient 3s misses remain visible; restored fixed-H completion is separate. CPU process percentages use one logical CPU=100, host CPU uses all logical CPUs=100. ActiveProcessorCount is not a CPU quota. Loopback JSON wire bytes exclude TCP/TLS overhead. TLS and WebSocket compression are disabled. Each run resets only this project's synthetic database with app stopped; seed and membership remain identical. Baseline repetitions precede candidate repetitions as required by branch workflow; thermal/order effects are limitations.
